Project Description:
ZSD is a Hydrometallurgical zinc smelter situated at Debari, about 13 kms from Udaipur in Raj., India. Commissioned in the yr 1968 with current production capacity 1 LTPA.
HZL is now proposing for “Expansion of Zinc Smelter (1 LTPA to 1.4 LTPA) through Modernization within the existing premises of ZSD under clause 7(ii) of EIA Notification 2006 amended from time to time at Villages: Debari & Bichhri, Tehsil: Girwa, District: Udaipur (Raj.).”
This expansion will be carried out in 2 phases, in 1st phase the capacity expansion will be achieved upto 1,20,000TPA (20%) through modernization with installation of state of art jumbo cell house, higher capacity reactors & thickeners in L&P section and Roaster. In the Phase-2, capacity will be further increased upto 1,40,000TPA (40%) by debottlenecking, improvement in current, melting efficiency & metal recovery.
This will result into improvement in metal recovery, recovery of minor metals & reduction in specific  power ,fresh water, GHG emission

Project Description:
"Constriction of Upper High-Level canal off taking from saddle dam No.1 of mahi dam, District Banswara (Rajasthan)”
There exists a dark zone in the project area where water is still a dream and the poor people and their lands are deprived of irrigation as well as drinking water. The tribal in-habitants of east-west region of Banswara, Sajjangarh, Kushalgarh, Anandpuri, Gangad Talai and Bagidora tehsil are still waiting for Mahi water. During draught years, the inhabitants of this area generally migrate to the neighboring states of Gujrat and M.P. for their livelihood whenever rains are low in this zone.
The proposed Upper High-Level Canal aims to utilize the available water of Mahi Dam in an efficient and equitable manner by providing assured irrigation to the high-level cultivable command areas presently deprived due to topographical constraints. The scheme will not only enhance agricultural productivity, cropping intensity and farmers’ income, but also support groundwater recharge.

Project Description:
ZSD is a Hydrometallurgical zinc smelter situated at Debari, about 13 kms from Udaipur in Raj., India. Commissioned in the yr 1968 with current production capacity 1 LTPA.
HZL is now proposing for “Expansion of Zinc Smelter (1 LTPA to 1.2 LTPA) through Modernization within the existing premises of ZSD under clause 7(ii) of EIA Notification 2006 amended from time to time at Villages: Debari & Bichhri, Tehsil: Girwa, District: Udaipur (Raj.).”
This expansion will be carried out in 2 phases, in 1st phase the capacity expansion will be achieved upto 1,20,000TPA (20%) through modernization with installation of state of art jumbo cell house, higher capacity reactors & thickeners in L&P section and Roaster. In the Phase-2, capacity will be further increased upto 1,40,000TPA (40%) by debottlenecking, improvement in current, melting efficiency & metal recovery.
This will result into improvement in metal recovery, recovery of minor metals & reduction in specific  power ,fresh water, GHG emission

Project Description: The Proposed area lies towards the south and southwestern part with respect to Khetri Copper belt hence there may be occurrence of Cu and REE mineralisations as several worker have reported gossans,old workings in the area. Four gravity highs in the area as inferred from Boguer gravity anomaly map. Considering its proximity to the Khetri copper mine and geophysical signatures a detailed survey was recommended in this zone. The zone Z-3 recommended by the NGPM work lies just towards south of this proposed block. STM work carried out by Rai (2023) has reported several old workings near Kakrana village and malachite staining within interbedded quartzite and phyllites of Bharkol Formation. The proposed block falls in gap area and no G-4 / G-3 work has been carried out till date. Under this background, it is therefore proposed to carry out a G-4 stage investigation in about 100 sq Km area around Boorka and Kalota areas to scan and establish the base metal mineralisation potential

Project Description:
On the basis of the outcome of the large scale mapping (LSM) carried out during FS: 2023-24, G3 level investigation is proposed in southwest of Mothoka area for FS: 2025-26 to study the subsurface nature of mineralisation. The area has undergone intense deformation, so it is proposed to carry out the detailed mapping in the area to know the control and nature of the mineralisation before planning of the boreholes.
It is proposed to carry out detailed mapping of 1.5 sq. km area on 1: 2,000 scale along with channel/BRS sampling. The mineralised zone of the western limb of a fold within interbedded dolomite will be targeted for drilling, while the eastern limb as well the hinge zone of the fold will be checked for mineralization through systematic sampling. Further subsurface exploration will be planned based on the outcome of surface sampling in the eastern limb and hinge zone.
Pitting or trenching will also be carried out in the soil covered area to check the continuity of the host rock

Project Description:
Geological mapping and reconnaissance surveys will be carried out in the Kalor, Jalore, and Bhinmal areas, Jalore District under the supervision of Shri Ishwar (Director, Geology), FS 2025-26.
The proposed area in toposheet 45C/11, western Rajasthan, lies within the Thar Desert and is mainly covered by aeolian and fluvial sands with patches of exposed basement rocks. The dominant lithology is Erinpura Granite (Neoproterozoic), along with Kailana Felsic Volcanics (rhyolite) and younger Malani Igneous Suite rocks, including Sankra Dykes.
Recent reconnaissance in nearby areas revealed high concentrations of strontium (up to 2343 ppm), niobium (up to 331 ppm), and TREE+Y (up to 1835 ppm), with enrichment in light REEs (La, Ce). Future work includes large-scale geological mapping (1:12,500 scale), subsurface drilling, trenching, and sampling to delineate mineralized zones. The area shows promising potential for REEs, base metals, lithium, and uranium, warranting detailed exploration.

Project Description: Geological mapping on 1:12,500 scale was carried out in 100 sq.km. area in and around Ambesar village, Bhilwara district, Rajasthan. Subsequently, a zone of copper mineralization was identified with 400 m length and 15-20 m width, on the surface, in the form of malachite, azurite and sulfides. Since, copper is an important base metal commodity, the objective of the current project is to establish the sub-surface continuity and estimate the resource of copper and associated mineralization. A total number of 6 boreholes (56 mm or 2.2 inch diameter boreholes) are proposed in this block.

Project Description:
Geological Mapping and Exploration for Tin in Wan Block, Sirohi District, Rajasthan

Geological mapping on a 1:2000 scale is planned over an area of 1.7 sq. km in and around Wan village of Sirohi district, Rajasthan (covering parts of toposheet no. 45C/16). During a previous preliminary survey, encouraging occurrences of Tin (Sn) were identified. This year, drilling is being undertaken in the Wan area to further investigate and confirm these promising findings.

Tin is considered a critical mineral and plays a vital role in green energy technologies. Therefore, the primary objective of this project is to establish sub-surface continuity and estimate the resource potential of Tin and associated mineralization.

The total area of the Wan Block is 1.7 sq. km. A total of 4 to 10 boreholes (each with a diameter of 56 mm) are proposed to be drilled. Some of these boreholes are located within the Laas Jhadoli Protected Forest Range in Sirohi district, Rajasthan.

Project Description: Geologically the block, SE of Mawri, falls in the parts of Siwana Ring complex of Malani Igneous Suite (Neo-Proterozoic age). It displays volcano-plutonic associations, anorogenic setting and potentials for REE and RM. During FS 2022-23, D.M of 1.5 sq km at 1:2000 scale  and drilling of 1250 m in 11 nos. of 1st level boreholes (inclined) as per MEMC guidelines were done. Overall 09 out of the 11 nos.  boreholes drilled in the area intersected significant REE lodes. Under G2 stage of exploration, a total 15 nos of 1st level boreholes are proposed at 100m interval with approximate depth of borehole about 115m as infilling boreholes in between already drilled boreholes. Based on results of 1st level boreholes, 13 nos. of 2nd level boreholes with approx. 195m depth are proposed to be planned at 200m interval. 04nos. 3rd level boreholes may be planned along the most successful profile lines with approximately 310m depth. Therefore, a total of 5500m of drilling is proposed in 30 boreholes.

The central Geological Programming Board (CGPB) has kindly approved one project namely Reconnaissance survey for copper and REE mineralization in and around Kalota and Boorka, Jhunjhunu district, Rajasthan. Project Description: G4 stage investigation is proposed for FS: 2025-26 to carry out reconnaissance survey by large scale mapping of 100 sq km area on 1: 12,500 scale around SirohiBhagoth area (Fig.-1) to search for potential zones of Copper and associated mineralization. The area is proposed for FS 2025-26 to assess the potentiality of Copper mineralization through scout drilling, pitting trenching, channel sampling, dug well dumps over 100 sq.km area. Ground water sampling in grid pattern is also proposed in the completely soil covered portion of the proposed area to check for elemental association important from mineralization point of view. Scout drilling of 300m is proposed in covered area is proposed to assess the subsurface nature and extension of the mineralized zone. Channel/groove samples and PTS are to be collected as per requirement and availability. In addition to study of thin sections, EPMA and XRD studies are also proposed to identify the various mineral phases.

Project Description: Geologically, the area is having basement of Malani Igneous suite of late Proterozoic age followed unconformably by early Jurassic Lathi Formation and middle Jurassic Jaisalmer Formation. Jaisalmer Formation is followed by early Cretaceous Sarnu Hill Formation and late Cretaceous Fatehgarh Formation. Cretaceous is followed by Akli and Mandai Formation of Palaeocene age and Kapurdi Formation of Eocene age. Eocene are followed by Pleistocene Phalsand Formation boulder spread, calcrete of subrecent Uttarlai Formation followed by recent alluvium and sand. The carbonatite/carbonatite veins are to be sampled systematically and the NGPM results will also be correlated with geological maps for delineating the host/target lithology. After target of  mineralization zone, 3 to 4 Nos. of scout inclined borehole will be planned to intersect the mineralization zone at 60m vertical depth.

Project Description:
The Ministry of Power vide its Notification dated 13.01.2023 has appointed  REC Power Development and Consultancy Limited to be the Bid Process Coordinator (BPC) for the purpose of selection of Bidder as Transmission Service Provider (TSP) to establish transmission system for “Transmission system for evacuation of power from REZ in Rajasthan (20 GW) under Phase-III Part I” through tariff based competitive bidding (TBCB) process.

Project Description:
The Construction of Thapra Anicut lift irrigation scheme across Anas River has been announced under Budget Announcement of Year 2023-24 Under Para No. 1731(3).

The total storage Capacity of the proposed Anicut is 135 Mcft. The Catchment area of the river between till the proposed site is 5381.37 sq.km. The design discharge is computed as 16102 cumec.
In View of lack of Irrigation facilities in non-command area of Anandpuri Block. It is proposed to construct Thapra anicut across Anas river with solar based Micro Irrigation Scheme in GP Thapra Tehsil Anandpuri Distt. Banswara. This project has been formulated with water allowance 5 cusecs/1000 Acre. According to this water allowance and available storage, 1450 Ha. area is taken to be irrigating through Micro Irrigation system.

The objective of the project is to assess the occurrence, quality and extent of Potash and associated minerals through geological mapping, sample collection and limited sub-surface exploration (Core Drilling). Exploration operations will include ground surveys, core drilling at selected locations and sampling. Only small temporary drill pads and access paths will be created as per requirement. Project Description:
The proposed Mor Sagar Reservoir is a critical water resource development project aimed at ensuring long term water security, drinking support and socio economic development of the surrounding region. The project location partly falls within forest land, which is unavoidable. Relocating the project outside the forest area is not feasible technically and would result, inadequate storage capacity and reduced project efficiency.  The Mor Sagar Reservoir is envisaged to cater to drinking water supply, 
groundwater recharge, and drought mitigation in a water-scarce region. The project serves a larger public interest, benefiting rural and semi-urban populations and supporting climate resilience. The proposal involves diversion of the bare minimum forest area, restricted strictly to the essential project components such as the dam embankment and reservoir submergence. Efforts have been made to avoid dense forest patches and minimize tree felling to the extent possible.

Project Description: M/s. UltraTech Cement Limited is proposing amendment in EC with respect to the timeline for Rainwater Harvesting & railway siding. Due to delay in commissioning of the project, adequate mine pit development for effective rainwater accumulation could not be achieved within the stipulated timeframe. Additionally, the project area under low rainfall, and the geology is characterized by thick alluvial/soil overburden (up to ~20 m) and highly fractured limestone formations, resulting in rapid percolation, seepage and negligible water retention, thereby limiting the effectiveness of rainwater harvesting within the specified timeline.  Further, the Ras–Bilara new railway line project announced by Indian Railways is presently in the early administrative and planning stages, though the survey has been completed. Due to the delay in finalization and execution of the proposed rail route, rail connectivity to the project site is also getting correspondingly delayed.

Village Dadikar, in particular, faces acute water shortages during the summer months, severely affecting drinking water availability, agriculture, and local livelihoods. 
In response to these challenges, NGO Sapna, with the support of its CSR partners, has previously facilitated the construction of two anicuts in Village Dadikar and one anicut in Village Bala Dehra. These interventions have led to a significant and visible transformation in the region over the past two years.
The proposed check dam will be constructed in Village Dadikar using an earthen bund combined with a central RCC structure to manage water force and ensure longevity.

Earthen Dam Specifications:
•	Bund Length: 130 meters (approx. 400 feet)
•	Height: 3.5 meters (approx. 10 feet)
•	Base Width: 24 meters (approx. 72 feet)
•	Top Width: 3.5 meters (approx.

The Brahmani Barrage Project constitutes the first phase of the broader river linking and water augmentation strategy. The project envisages construction of a barrage across the Brahmani River, a tributary of the Chambal River, situated upstream of the Jawahar Sagar Dam.

In future surplus water availability in Brahamani will be diverted though gravity flow into Bisalpur Dam, fulfil future drinking water demands of Jaipur.

Project Description:
The widening and construction of State Highway-32 from Salumber to Banswara, a total length of 93 km, to a 2-lane configuration with paved shoulders is proposed under the project.

This corridor is an important transportation route that originates at Salumber and terminates at its junction with NH-56 at Banswara. Further, NH-927A provides connectivity to the Delhi–Mumbai Expressway (NE-4) through feeder interchanges in Madhya Pradesh, making it a key high-speed transportation corridor for the region.

The Salumber–Banswara section of SH-32 provides vital connectivity between Southern Rajasthan and the major cities of Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat, including Ratlam, Indore, Dhar, Ahmedabad, Vadodara, and Surat, through NH-56 and NH-927A. The project is expected to significantly enhance regional connectivity, facilitate the movement of passengers and goods, and contribute to the socio-economic development of the area.

The objective of the project is to assess the occurrence, quality and extent of Potash and associated minerals through geological mapping, sample collection and limited sub-surface exploration (Core Drilling). Exploration operations will include ground surveys, core drilling at selected locations and sampling. Only small temporary drill pads and access paths will be created as per requirement. Project Description:
Geological mapping on a 1:2,000 scale was carried out over 1.5 sq. km in and around the Guranal area, Balotra District, Rajasthan (part of Toposheet No. 45C/6). Based on the encouraging results, G-3 stage exploration, comprising detailed mapping and drilling, was undertaken during Field Season 2022–23, leading to the delineation of promising REE and associated mineralization. To establish the subsurface continuity and upgrade the resource confidence, G-2 stage exploration has been planned during Field Season 2026–27 over 0.8 sq. km.

As REEs are critical and strategic minerals essential for clean energy and advanced technologies, exploration in the Siwana Ring Complex has been accorded high priority by the Ministry of Mines, Government of India. The proposed G-2 programme envisages 32 vertical boreholes, of which 04 boreholes (57 mm or 2.24-inch diameter) fall within the Siwana Protected Forest and require prior forest clearance.

Project Description:
A G4 stage exploration was carried out by GSI during FS 2019–20 in the Saloli- Buchpuri area. The area around Saloli and Buchpuri villages was identified as a potential block for graphite mineralization. Considering the strategic importance of graphite and the need to assess its subsurface continuity and resource potential, GSI has proposed a G3 stage project (Saloli–Buchpuri Block) for graphite exploration during Field Season 2026–27.

The Saloli–Buchpuri Block covers a total area of 2.00 sq. km, of which approximately 0.44 sq. km falls within the Saloli Protected Forest. To assess the subsurface continuity and thickness of the graphite-bearing horizons, six boreholes (56 mm or 2.2-inch diameter) have been proposed within the block. Out of these six proposed boreholes, five fall within the Protected Forest area. The proposed drilling is aimed at delineating the graphite mineralization at depth and evaluating its resource potential.
